subject: chemistry
question_text: Define bond order. Show that the He₂ molecule does not exist.

verification.note: PREDICTED, not asked. This question comes from the enumeration sweep: the book uses bond order inside its MO long answer but never asks the definition or the standard He₂ non-existence check that NCERT teaches with it. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. AI chemistry check 2026-08-25. Reworded one common mistake that read as if Nb − Na were the wrong subtraction order; the He₂ configuration, the Nb/Na counts and the bond-order arithmetic all verified correct.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
lines: Bond order: half the difference between
the number of electrons in bonding
steps.why: Each bonding pair adds a bond and each antibonding pair cancels one, so halving the difference counts the net number of bonds.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the half. Two electrons make one bond, so the difference is halved.
Subtracting the wrong way round. The correct order is bonding minus antibonding, Nb − Na, never Na − Nb.
steps.memory_tip: Net electrons that bond, divided by two per bond.
steps.margin_note: Define Nb and Na in words beside the formula.

steps.label: He₂ calculation
lines: He₂ would have 4 electrons: σ1s² σ*1s²

lines.text: Bond order zero — He₂ does not exist

steps.why: The antibonding pair cancels the bonding pair completely, so there is no net bond to hold the two atoms together.
common_mistakes: Filling all four electrons into σ1s. The orbital holds two; the next two go to σ*1s.
Concluding a weak bond. Bond order zero means NO bond, not a weak one.
steps.memory_tip: Two in, two against, nothing left — no molecule.
steps.margin_note: Write the configuration, the two counts, then the boxed conclusion.

insider_note: Definition and calculation, one mark each, and the calculation mark is really its conclusion. Reaching bond order zero is not the answer; the line saying He₂ therefore does not exist is.
